SddInfra.keywords: infra, infrastructure, tooling, tool-stack, dev-workflow, verification-commands, decision-log, sdd-infra
SddInfra.Mission:
Author or evolve an `infrastructure` scope spec — the project's tooling: package manager, type-checker, linter, formatter, test runner, git hooks, CI. A self-contained living spec: Vision, Tool Stack (Decision Log per tool), Dev Workflow Example, File Structure, Effective Rules, Verification Commands, Bootstrap Requirements, Handoff to scaffold. Loaded lazily by the router; inherits the router core (language, dialogue, safeguard, diverge, no-narration, stateless) — not repeated here.
Input — scope name + intent (or an existing spec for refine / pivot). Output — `specs//.spec.md` (scope-type infrastructure). The router sends product / library to the scope branch and interface to the interface branch.
Out of scope: product / library design, module decomposition. The project portal is the root branch.
**Glossary.** Modes: greenfield · refine · pivot · rewrite. Mandatory tool categories: vcs, package-management, git-hooks. Optional: type-check, linting, formatting, test-unit, test-e2e, bundler, ci, monorepo-tool, docs.

BeliefState.deps: AX_OPERATOR_LANGUAGE, AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE, AX_DIALOGUE_DISCIPLINE, AX_OPERATOR_SAFEGUARD, AX_NO_PROCESS_NARRATION, AX_STATELESS_ARTIFACT, AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH

SddInfra.BeliefState:
Inherited from the loading directive (already in context): AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND, AX_PROGRESSIVE_DISCLOSURE, MESSAGE_LAYOUT, QUESTION_RULE_SLIM, SESSION_FILE_FORMAT
Each directive runs in one of several modes, auto-detected from operator intake. Mode controls step branching and which axioms apply. The concrete mode set is directive-specific (e.g. `greenfield` / `refine` / `pivot`; `initial` / `extend-dag`; `initial` / `add-module` / `refine-module`).
Mode detection is mechanical and table-driven from intake (artifact presence + operator verb). Ambiguous intake never defaults silently → HALT and ask the operator (binary disambiguation where possible). The detection table is directive-specific.
The `scope` flow reads `specs/README.md` for project context (vision, scope graph, sibling scopes). It MUST NOT rewrite the file. The narrow exception (per the `root` flow's `AX_PORTAL_PRIMARY_OWNER`): when the `scope` flow creates a brand-new scope, it MAY append one placeholder row to the Scopes table tagged `🚧 (awaiting root sync)`. Any other edit is forbidden — run the `root` flow instead.
The scope spec is a living document. In `refine` mode any section may be updated in place. There is no frozen 7 Handoff — the Handoff section evolves as modules are added.
`pivot` uses one-line Decision Log supersession: preserve the old entry; append a new `-DL-N` entry whose parenthetical carries the old→new delta, `supersedes: `, and the pre-rework git ref. The spec body is rewritten in place; git history is the full predecessor.
A spec lives in two states. **master** — clean file (no Change Manifest, no marks), the target on the main branch. **review-state** — the same file on a working branch during a change: the target text is written IN PLACE (everything else byte-for-byte, so the branch diff reads like a normal PR), with the temporary change manifest loaded by the owning authoring flow at the top and affected lines marked `✚` (new) / `~` (changed). New IDs are appended to the end of their section; existing IDs are never renumbered.
`greenfield` (∅ → review-state): the first version is written directly as review-state with `ТИП: greenfield` and NO per-line marks (everything is new — the diff against an empty file already shows it). `refine` / `pivot` edit an existing master in place WITH marks.
The spec change is a reviewable PR (design-PR). Before the internal critic, finalize semantic bytes (Decision Log compression including merge/delete, ID collision repair, pivot supersession), then obtain the operator's delta-only final hierarchy Approval. The critic loop is necessary but NOT sufficient and owns one global five-result cap across any correction/finalization return; such a return preserves its scratch and next round number. Critic target/write ownership stays specs-only; the separate VCS publication-set may add only mechanically attributed durable authoring outputs (registered research, canonical portal/index files, and the exact session-ignore addition), and any other dirty path halts. After the critic, approve only its actual delta, remove review scaffolding with Critic Rounds last, and pass the final-byte integrity check. Publish exactly the role-validated clean publication-set bytes. External approval names one reviewed commit; merge that same commit with no semantic rewrite afterward. Implementation (scaffold → execute) follows the merged master.
Reconcile has one narrow non-semantic exception: an explicitly classified editorial correction (spelling, formatting, or a mechanical link correction to an already-defined target) may use its frozen task-free target-set plus exact `sdd-check --all` direct receipt. It must change no GOAL, requirement, behaviour, contract, inventory, architecture, dependency, BDD acceptance, risk, or Decision Log meaning. Any such delta is semantic and returns to the authoring + integrated review lifecycle above before scaffold/reopen/execute.
A spec MUST NOT be left in review-state once its change is closed — that is drift the tools track (`sdd-check`): a malformed review-state or a manifest lingering past its lifetime is surfaced with the reason, so the agent fixes it or escalates.
Phase reads specs only, never code; no project-wide search (grep / find / ripgrep) outside the reads explicitly listed by the directive. `audit` is the only directive permitted to read code; it alone resolves spec/code mismatch.
For scope-type=infrastructure:
**Tool categories — two classes.** Mandatory: vcs, package-management, git-hooks. Optional: type-check, linting, formatting, test-unit, test-e2e, test-ui, bundler, ci, monorepo-tool, docs. The agent proposes a subset from intent. Mandatory categories cannot be dropped.
**vcs is always mandatory.** Resolves to `ai/directives/infra/git-setup.xml`.
**Per tool category: 2–3 candidates with trade-offs.** Operator picks → Mandatory Rationale Pull → Decision Log entry. No tool may be locked without a Decision Log entry.
**Tool interaction check.** After every tool is chosen, verify compatibility (linter vs formatter, test runner vs type-check, CI vs package manager).
**Effective rules derived from tools.** After tool stack is finalized, look up each chosen tool in `ai/directives/knowledge.xml` `` section: find every rule whose `` match the tool name or its config artefacts. Record matched rule `` paths in spec Effective Rules. Missing-rule handling: governed by `AX_SCOPE_RULES_DECLARATION` (in-session operator pick — skip / research-and-author / defer).
**Dev workflow example is required.** The spec includes a Developer Workflow Example (shell-script shape) before final approval.
In AI-first development, an e2e test against the live runtime (not mocks) is a mandatory verification category for a feature, not an optional add-on an agent may quietly drop. Unit + lint are the floor a feature cannot ship without; e2e is what earns confidence that the floor actually holds end to end. `test-e2e` is never screened out by the agent's own hypothesis ("small task, skip it") — it is picked or waived by an explicit operator decision. When live e2e is genuinely impossible for this task, unit coverage alone is acceptable, but only as a NAMED decision carrying a one-line risk statement in the Decision Log — never a silent omission.
An e2e test picked over unit-only carries its own closing bar: it is not DONE until it also captures its proof screenshots at each key point of the flow (`AX_E2E_PROOF_SCREENSHOT_ALWAYS`, `ai/directives/testing/playwright-e2e.xml`) — a live e2e run with no screenshot trail is unverifiable evidence, no better than the "small task, skip it" shortcut this axiom forbids.
Every non-obvious decision → a Decision Log entry in `DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT` — one line, the expanded part in parentheses: `-DL-N — (почему: …; отвергнуто: …; риск: …)`; IDs are stable. Non-obvious only (`AX_DECISION_LOG_NON_OBVIOUS`): a pick already recorded in the spec's own tables is never duplicated as a DL row. Which decisions qualify and which Decision Log receives the entry are specified per directive.
In `pivot` mode, preserve the prior entry byte-for-byte and append one new one-line `-DL-N — (...)` entry; its parenthetical names the old→new delta, `supersedes: `, and the git ref for the pre-rework state. The prior id may be a legacy `D-N` only when it already existed; never rewrite append-only history just to rename it. Pivot Invalidation List enumerates downstream artifacts requiring `refine-module` / reopen — consumed by `audit` via `AX_STALE_AFTER_PIVOT_VERIFICATION`.
`rewrite` mode is the exception: a pre-production / v0 scope with no production backing, whose old content was scratch that helps nothing going forward. It replaces the spec from a clean slate — NO supersession trail, NO Pivot Invalidation List (nothing downstream to keep coherent; git history is the only record). Use `pivot` (keep the trail) whenever the scope has any production backing or downstream consumers; use `rewrite` only for genuine v0 throwaway. Enforcement: a scope that already has downstream artifacts on disk (module specs or task tickets) is by definition NOT v0 — `rewrite` is forbidden there; halt and use `pivot`.
Scope-wide rules are declared in spec Rules. Categories with directory mapping: - coding → `ai/directives/coding/.xml` - testing → `ai/directives/testing/.xml` - architecture → `ai/directives/architecture/.xml` - infra → `ai/directives/infra/.xml`
Every rule reference must resolve to an existing file. Missing → operator picks resolution IN-SESSION (never a halt, never an autonomous task): - **skip** — tool's own defaults are the discipline; record in Decision Log. - **research-and-author** — agent WebFetches authoritative docs (official source from `package.json#homepage` or operator-supplied URL), drafts rule file, operator approves before write to `ai/directives//.xml`. Drafts capture TIMELESS engineering practice only — discipline, trade-offs, anti-pattern categories, binary invariants. NOT captured: version numbers, CLI flags, config-syntax snippets, plugin lists (those churn between releases; they live in `package.json` / config files). - **defer** — record as Open Risk in Handoff with `Owner: operator-action`; proceed.
Operator refuses to choose → `H_MISSING_RULE_FILE`. Otherwise no halt.
**Every rule activates through an explicit operator decision — never silently.** The decision is two-staged: Stage A locks the relevance shortlist per category with the operator; Stage B walks the axioms of `architecture/*` and `infra/*` rules for Accept (default) / Adapt / Override. Every deviation from a rule default lands in the Decision Log. `coding/*` / `testing/*` rules stay deferred — the phase-subagent loads them at phase entry per `phase-execution-protocol`.
Scope spec declares `depends-on` edges in Scope Dependencies. These edges feed cascade computation in the `scaffold` flow. Cross-scope contracts are sourced from `interface`-type scopes — never described inside a product scope spec.
Introducing a parallel mechanism where an existing one from a neighbour spec could be extended is a decision at GOAL level, never a silent author call. "Вводим новое" is a valid answer ONLY when it names the specific neighbour invariant / requirement ID the existing mechanism cannot satisfy, and records the choice as its own Decision Log entry (`DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT`) citing that ID. No cited ID, no entry → the mechanism stays unjustified: route it back to the operator as an open question, not a decision already made on their behalf. This governs the AUTHOR's system-fit check (`STEP_*_SYSTEM_FIT` in `scope` / `module` / `interface` / `infra`); `AX_REUSE_FIRST` runs the same bias against duplication from the CRITIC's reactive vantage, after the artifact already exists — the two apply one belief at two different points in the lifecycle, not two competing rules.
Separate Facts / Assumptions / Hypotheses in every intake-style frame. - **Facts** — directly observable from input artifacts (spec, sibling specs, rule files, extracted measurements). - **Assumptions** — working assumptions awaiting confirmation; mark explicitly. - **Hypotheses** — conjectures that require operator validation before they are promoted to requirements.
Conflating the three causes downstream decisions to be made on unvalidated assumptions, producing requirements mismatches that surface only at integration; surface them in distinct lists.
External research (WebSearch/WebFetch) run in this session ALWAYS lands as a research document via `npx gennady sdd-new research --scope --slug ` — filled in BEFORE the result feeds a proposal to the operator; a chat summary is not storage (session dies, research dies with it). Every factual claim must be re-verifiable: traced to a source (a specific page, URL + access date; for code-derived facts — path + commit) OR explicitly flagged `agent conclusion` / `from model memory as of `. A fact carrying neither is a document defect, not a style choice. A repeat question checks existing `specs/**/research/` first — supersede, never duplicate.
Prefer primary evidence: official documentation, repository/release notes, standards, or papers. A secondary comparison may supplement but never solely support a tool/version/API decision. The candidate analysis remains immutable after it is shown. Once the operator decides, update only `FINAL_DISPOSITION`: outcome, the actual spec/Decision Log choice, and its delta from the research recommendation. A later critic change updates the same disposition or marks the document superseded.
Discovery is design-blind to repository code (per `AX_SPEC_IS_SOLE_SOURCE`) **except** inside the External Dependencies Audit step, where narrow Read is permitted **only for inventory verification** — confirming whether a referenced package, file, scope, or tool physically exists. Permitted reads there: `package.json` and equivalents, `tsconfig.json` and equivalents, `specs/README.md`, sibling scope manifests, filesystem existence checks. Forbidden there: reading application source code to influence design decisions — inventory verification answers "does X exist", never "how does X work internally". An existing mechanism this audit turns up — one the spec should extend instead of duplicating — MUST feed back into the design: revising Architecture / Contracts on that finding is the ordinary continuation of THIS session's drafting, not a separate ceremony, as long as the spec has not yet merged to master (`AX_PIVOT_REQUIRES_SUPERSESSION` governs a revision raised after that point). Pop back to the relevant earlier step explicitly, incorporate the finding, then re-run the External Dependencies Audit once more before writing the final spec.
Every infra spec carries at least one diagram in an `Overview` section, high up — the developer workflow or tool pipeline at a glance, one glance beats a paragraph. The floor is one (mermaid or ASCII), held by tooling: `sdd-check` fails a missing section (`SDD_NO_DIAGRAM_BLOCK`) or an empty one (`SDD_DIAGRAM_BLOCK_EMPTY`). Beyond the floor the author adds more views by judgment; that is not a gate.
Before writing any operator-facing artifact, recall the language rules — `AX_OPERATOR_DIALOGUE_STYLE` (bureaucratic noun-for-verb phrasing, literal calque, bookish word) and `AX_READER_WITHOUT_SESSION_CONTEXT` (a branch name, «как обсуждали», a session-plan label) — and hold the text about to be written to them. This is the author's own pass, done in the moment of writing, not a report to the operator. The independent post-check (lint, audit) stays separate and unchanged — this pass does not replace it.
A mutation is not done until its scope passes the mechanical check. Any flow that creates or evolves an artifact under a scope — spec, module, ticket, DAG, tracker — closes by running `sdd-check` on the affected scope (`sdd-check --all specs/`; portal, task-DAG, tracker, or cross-scope work → `sdd-check --all .`) and resolving or consciously deferring every finding before handing off.
SddInfra.HaltConditions: | 🛑 ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_NO_INTAKE` | Empty intake | | `H_AMBIGUOUS_MODE` | Spec exists + mode verb absent (per `AX_MODE_AUTO_DETECT_OR_HALT`) | | `H_MANDATORY_CATEGORY_DROPPED` | A mandatory category (vcs / package-management / git-hooks) was dropped | | `H_SYSTEM_FIT_NOT_RUN` | `STEP_2_TOOL_CATEGORIES` entered before `STEP_1B_SYSTEM_FIT`'s checklist closed, or "вводим новое" recorded without the specific neighbour invariant/requirement ID it fails (`AX_PARALLEL_MECHANISM_REQUIRES_JUSTIFICATION`) | | `H_TOOL_LOCKED_WITHOUT_DECISION` | A tool locked without a Decision Log entry | | `H_MISSING_RULE_FILE` | A rule reference does not resolve to an existing file | | `H_PIVOT_NO_INVALIDATION_LIST` | `pivot` mode without a Pivot Invalidation List | | `H_REWRITE_WITH_DOWNSTREAM` | `rewrite` mode but the scope already has tickets — not v0, use `pivot` (`AX_PIVOT_REQUIRES_SUPERSESSION`) | | `H_BOOTSTRAP_REQUIREMENTS_MISSING` | External-deps step finished without a Bootstrap Requirements section | | `H_OPERATOR_REJECT` | Operator rejected the spec |

Step.Action: State from the router gives the portal + scope-type (infrastructure). Resolve the scope name; stat the spec → `greenfield` or detect the mode per `AX_DIRECTIVE_MODE` / `AX_MODE_AUTO_DETECT_OR_HALT`. The registry answers "what knowledge exists" in ONE deterministic `Read ai/directives/knowledge.xml` — it is the sole index (`` section) and lists every rule file's exact path (`ai/directives//.xml`) with ``; per `AX_SCOPE_RULES_DECLARATION` a category with no matching entry maps to `ai/directives//.xml` directly. `ls`/`find` over `ai/directives/**` is not needed — the registry already answers that in one read; a directory scan is a wasted turn against a known index.

Step.Goal: Confirm scope-type and the operating scale.
Step.Action: Confirm scope-type (`infrastructure`) and mode with the operator. The section set is NOT an Ask — it is fixed by `INFRASTRUCTURE_SPEC_STRUCTURE` and materialized by `sdd-new` at STEP_7; naming the skeleton to the operator here would be asking approval for a contract, not a decision they own. State the confirmed default SCALE inline in the plan text instead of a standalone question — `module` for a typical infra scope unless intake signals otherwise (`AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH`) — and let the operator correct it here or at the next substantive Ask (STEP_2); it never burns a dedicated round. If state already resolves every field, proceed without Ask.

Step.Goal: Reconcile with the existing system before tool categories are declared.
Step.Action:
FIRST action this step: run orientation ToolCall below (this works even before `sdd-new` materializes the infra spec) and read its output in full: the portal line, the one-hop neighbours with their paths, entity/contract NAMES, requirement IDs + titles, the consumers list, and its closing question.
Then close, in THIS message, the fixed checklist — record every answer in the spec (Decision Log entry when (a)/(b) lands on "new", inline note otherwise): (a) Is the tooling mechanism this scope is about to stand up already an existing kind — does the extract already name a sibling infra scope (e.g. `infra-base`) that owns it? (b) If not: which existing infra scope / mechanism the extract names are we EXTENDING instead of introducing a parallel pipeline / config / gate? (c) Which neighbour specs (paths, from the extract) will need work for this tool stack to fit the system — each becomes its own «СОСЕДИ» line in the eventual `CHANGE_MANIFEST` / Pivot Invalidation List sideways entry? (d) Which neighbour requirements (IDs, from the extract) conflict with the tool categories we are about to declare, and how is the conflict resolved? "Вводим новое" answers (a)/(b) ONLY together with the specific neighbour invariant/requirement ID the existing mechanism cannot satisfy, plus its own Decision Log entry (`AX_PARALLEL_MECHANISM_REQUIRES_JUSTIFICATION`) — else `H_SYSTEM_FIT_NOT_RUN`. On a genuinely greenfield project with no neighbours, `sdd-orient` degenerates to its one-line "соседей нет" — the checklist still runs, (a) still gets an honest answer, (c)/(d) collapse to "н/д"; the step itself is never skipped. STOP. npx gennady sdd-orient --scope Inputs : =operator-confirmed infrastructure scope retained by this flow. Use orientation.

Step.Goal: Declare the tool categories, then route on stack typicality.
Step.Action:
Propose a subset from intent per `AX_INFRASTRUCTURE_FLOW`, Facts / Assumptions / Hypotheses separated per `AX_EVIDENCE_HYGIENE`.
Already-approved categories are session input, not a question: a category+tool pair the operator already locked earlier this session — root's `STEP_3_INFRA_BOOTSTRAP` Tool Stack table, or an earlier round of this very flow — is read from state and shown back as ONE reference line, e.g. «уже утверждено: npm, tsc, eslint+prettier, vitest, husky — не переспрашиваю», never re-run through research and never re-asked. Only categories still unlocked (a mandatory one split out on its own, e.g. git-hooks, or an optional one like vite / test-e2e / ci) go through the research-and-Ask cycle below. Reopening an already-locked tool needs a concrete conflict THIS discovery found — then it is its own flagged question naming the reason (` не подходит из-за — заменить на ?`), never a silent whole-table re-confirm.
Mandatory categories (vcs / package-management / git-hooks) cannot be dropped (`H_MANDATORY_CATEGORY_DROPPED`). `test-e2e` is optional on the category LIST but not on the DECISION — per `AX_E2E_FIRST` the agent proposes it in by default and takes an explicit operator answer to drop it (with the risk line recorded), rather than reasoning "small scope, skip e2e" on its own and folding that into the proposed subset unchallenged.
- WHEN every still-unlocked proposed category resolves to an already-known registry rule (`ai/directives/knowledge.xml` names a matching `` entry for each — no exotic / novel tool named by the operator, no operator request for a detailed pass) -> EXPRESS branch below replaces the full interview for STEP_2/STEP_3 - WHEN a still-unlocked category has no registry match, or the operator asked for "подробно" / a detailed pass, or typicality is genuinely unclear -> run the full operator interview — `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/interview-protocol.directive.xml")` — passing scope-type `infrastructure` (selects the TopicCatalog block) and the confirmed `scale:` from the session file: per `AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH` `fix` / `function` → base topics + the triage minimum; `product` → the full scope-type block. The interview IS the substance of the step; STEP_3 then runs in full, over the still-unlocked categories only. Uncertain typicality defaults to THIS branch — never a silent EXPRESS guess.
If every category is already locked (the reference line above covers the whole set), STEP_2 and STEP_3 are done with no research and no Ask at all — proceed to STEP_4.
EXPRESS branch (typical stack): run the STEP_3 research gate now, for every still-unlocked category at once (2–3 targeted WebSearch queries per category — alive/current, AI-agent friendliness for the current year). Per `AX_RESEARCH_PERSISTED`, before the candidates table below is shown, persist the findings with researchManifest ToolCall below, filled (STATUS/PROBLEM/CRITERIA/OPTIONS/DECISION/CONSEQUENCES/EVIDENCE/RELATED), one document per category or one covering the batch. Then present ONE batch Ask — a single candidates table, one row per still-unlocked category (an already-locked category never gets a row — it already had its reference line above), each row naming the recommended tool + a one-line rationale from the research (not recall) + a currency note, per `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND`, plus a link to the research document backing it. The operator confirms the whole table or names deviations in ONE reply. Include the Tool Interaction Check (linter vs formatter, runner vs type-check, CI vs package manager) in this first batch. A deviation opens a follow-up only when its consequences create a new unresolved interaction; otherwise apply it directly. One Ask normally replaces the per-category STEP_2 / STEP_3 interview cycle — Mandatory Rationale Pull → Decision Log entry per `AX_DECISION_LOG_REQUIRED` still applies per tool (`H_TOOL_LOCKED_WITHOUT_DECISION`), its RELATED citing the research document in parentheses: the compression is in the NUMBER of operator round-trips, never in the Decision Log discipline. For any locked tool that is a GATE tool, the same Integration Detail concreteness bar as STEP_3 applies — no exemption for having taken the fast path. STEP_3 is done once this closes — proceed to STEP_4. STOP only when that Ask was needed. Inputs , : this STEP_2 category context. npx gennady sdd-new research --scope --slug Use researchManifest.

Step.Goal: Choose a tool per category (full path only — EXPRESS already closed this step).
Step.Action:
Skip entirely when STEP_2 took the EXPRESS branch — its two Asks already produced the candidates table, the operator pick, and the Tool Interaction Check; re-running this step would re-ask what STEP_2 just closed. Otherwise (full path): this step runs over the still-unlocked categories only — STEP_2's reference line already excluded every category the operator locked in root's bootstrap or an earlier round, and none of those get a row, research, or an Ask here. Research gate before candidates — applies to still-unlocked categories being picked NOW (`greenfield`, or `refine`/`pivot` touching a category not already locked in the spec); skip it also for a `fix`/`module`-scale session where the category is already locked in the existing infra spec, per `AX_SCALE_PROPORTIONAL_DEPTH` — no revisit, no research. In every case, reopening a locked category requires a concrete conflict discovery surfaced, raised as its own named-reason question, never a silent re-confirm. Where it applies: run 2–3 targeted WebSearch queries per category under revision — is each candidate alive and current (not abandoned / superseded), and how it compares on AI-agent friendliness for the current year (text-configurable, autofix, machine-readable diagnostics) — before drafting candidates from memory. Per `AX_RESEARCH_PERSISTED`, before candidates are presented, persist the findings — researchManifest ToolCall below, filled (STATUS/PROBLEM/CRITERIA/OPTIONS/DECISION/CONSEQUENCES/EVIDENCE/RELATED). Then per category, 2–3 candidates with trade-offs per `AX_DIVERGE_BEFORE_RECOMMEND` (reach past the obvious default; judge against THIS project); for each candidate presented, one line stating why it's here per the research (not recall) plus the source, and a currency / AI-friendliness note, plus a link to the research document backing the category. If WebSearch is unavailable in this environment, say so plainly instead of silently falling back — `предлагаю по памяти на <дата обучения модели>, ресёрч недоступен` — a named caveat, not silence (no research document in that case — nothing was found to persist).
For a GATE tool — anything the execution phases' own verification gate enforces (linter, formatter, type-checker, test runner, contract-lint): the Integration Detail fields (`Версия/API` · `Нужные методы` · `Эскиз интеграции` · `Ограничения`, already in the Tool Stack skeleton) MUST carry what a phase worker needs to write its config with ZERO further research — the exact locked version, the config schema's version/URL, a literal config skeleton (even minimal), and any known version-specific gotcha (a default that changed between majors, a file type the tool does not handle out of the box). When this concrete detail is not already in evidence, it is exactly what the research gate above exists to produce — persist the schema URL/version and the skeleton in the research document (`AX_RESEARCH_PERSISTED`), never leave it for the execute-phase worker to reverse-engineer from the installed package's internals (`phase-execution-protocol` STEP_3B_TOOL_API already forbids that path on the worker's side — this step is where the gap is meant to close instead).
Operator picks → Mandatory Rationale Pull → Decision Log entry per `AX_DECISION_LOG_REQUIRED` (`DECISION_LOG_ENTRY_FORMAT`), its RELATED citing the research document in parentheses; no tool locked without one (`H_TOOL_LOCKED_WITHOUT_DECISION`). Tool Interaction Check (linter vs formatter, runner vs type-check, CI vs package manager). STOP. npx gennady sdd-new research --scope --slug Inputs , : =operator-confirmed infrastructure scope; =short restricted slug for this STEP_3 tool comparison. Use researchManifest.
Shell-script shape: how a developer installs, checks, tests, commits. STOP.

Step.Goal: Lock file layout, Effective Rules, Verification Commands.
Step.Action: Repo root layout + config-file mapping. Effective Rules — activate per `AX_RULE_ACTIVATION`: look up each chosen tool in the rule registry per `AX_SCOPE_RULES_DECLARATION`; Stage A — shortlist «recommend activate» + «considered, recommend skip» with one-line rationales, operator locks the list; Stage B — for `infra/*` rules on the locked list read only `Mission`, `Belief_State`, `Reward_Criteria` and walk the axioms: operator Accept (default) / Adapt / Override, the latter two → Decision Log. Record matched rule file paths (unresolvable reference → `H_MISSING_RULE_FILE`). When a formatter is among the chosen tools, default its ignore file (`.prettierignore` / Biome `ignore`) to EXCLUDE `specs/` (and the legacy v1 `tasks/`, when present mid-migration) — agent-authored markdown; formatter churn there breaks table alignment and produces noisy diffs unrelated to the change. Record the exclusion in the spec's own Effective Rules so it is not a silent tool-config fact. `.gitignore` MUST also default to cover `.claude/tmp/` — the shared scratch directory execution workers use for temp/trial files (`AX_PERMITTED_BASH_COMMANDS`), reused across roles and unrelated to any one tool choice — recorded in the same Effective Rules entry, never a silent omission. Verification Commands table — one row per active tool command. STOP.

Walk the drafted spec; extract external assumptions; classify `exists` | `missing` | `unknown` (narrow read for inventory only, per `AX_BOOTSTRAP_NARROW_READ` and `AX_SPEC_IS_SOLE_SOURCE` — design stays sourced from specs); resolve with the operator; record confirmed cross-scope assumptions as `depends-on` edges per `AX_CROSS_SCOPE_DEPENDENCIES`; materialize the canonical six-column Bootstrap Requirements table. Every task-owned `package` row names exact `package.json, package-lock.json` Gate Artifacts. The infrastructure scope that first installs dependencies must own Node/npm runtime artifacts (`.nvmrc`, Node fields in `package.json`, `.npmrc`) before that install. For project-readiness work, record exact `Readiness Gates` and repo-relative `Gate Artifacts`; use `—` for non-readiness rows. ArtifactOutput.Contract:
One line per entry — no Status/Recorded fields, no multi-line block. The parenthetical carries only what applies; omit a clause entirely rather than writing it empty.
```markdown -DL-N — (почему: ; отвергнуто: ; риск: ) ```
**ID.** `-DL-` — spec acronym first, exactly like a Task-ID and like `-REQ-` (`REQUIREMENT_ENTRY_FORMAT`); `` is sequential within THIS spec only — the acronym gives global uniqueness, not the number. This is the only grammar for NEW entries. Existing append-only file-local `D-N` entries remain immutable and resolvable as legacy references; never create another; conflicts (a duplicate number inside one spec) are caught mechanically, the same way as for `-REQ-`.
Superseding a prior decision appends `; supersedes: -DL-M` to the parenthetical instead of a separate field — the entry stays one line. `` is the recording date (`YYYY-MM-DD`); status (active / superseded / rejected / deferred) is implicit from prose and from whether a later entry supersedes this one — a spec has no dangling "rejected" or "deferred" entries sitting as if active, the prose says so directly (e.g. `отвергнуто в пользу X` folded into the same line that would have recorded it, never a standalone rejected entry with its own `-DL-N`).
